principle_violations.reason: The Order class directly manages item data, including items, quantities, and prices. It is responsible for multiple domain concepts, such as managing order data and processing payment, which should ideally be separated.
principle_violations.suggestion: Decompose the Order class to separate responsibilities. Create a separate class to manage order items and their details. The Order class should only aggregate and manage a list of those item objects.
code: public void addItem(String name, int quantity, double price) { ... }

principle_violations.reason: The PaymentProcessor interface requires implementing classes to define both pay and auth_sms methods. Not all payment processors need SMS authentication.
principle_violations.suggestion: Split the PaymentProcessor interface into smaller, more specific interfaces. For instance, create an interface for SMS authentication and another for basic payment processing, and let each concrete class implement only those interfaces it needs.
code: public abstract void auth_sms(Order order, String code);
